title: A commit from a checkout behind its moved branch is refused
why: Lane notes-fix-guard-2: three resumed agents kept a stale index or tree after their branch moved (coordinator, 17:07 CST Nov 7). The harm is a silent undo of pushed work.
note: Related steps: one-worktree-per-branch, checkout-b-current-branch. Done check: a red test where a commit from a checkout behind its moved branch is refused, and a fast-forward pull still passes. Absorbs proposed steps one-branch-one-worktree (lane past-ruling-on-send) and one-branch-per-writer (lane reviewer-no-session-tools), coordinator 18:19 CST Nov 7. Incident: a lane ran three writer agents in parallel on one branch, each in its own worktree; two hit stale indexes after the branch moved, and those indexes staged a reversal of hooks/guard.py (both caught before commit). Add a red test where a commit whose index differs from HEAD's tree beyond the staged paths is refused or warned. Lane, 18:20 CST: the added case is covered by decision stale-tree-commit (on branch lane/resumed-agent-stale-tree). A commit is refused, not warned, when a staged path holds the copy from the pre-move commit (read from the HEAD reflog) that the move changed. Fourth incident, folded by the coordinator at 19:14 CST Nov 7 (proposed step brief-branch-held): lane report-model-from-role briefed two agents onto one branch, lane/rmfr-build, at 18:40 CST, and one worktree got foreign staging. Add a refusal for a brief whose checkout -B names a branch another live worktree holds.
